Title: August 10, 2023 - Boulder City Council Special Meeting (Board and Commission Appointments) and Study Session (University Hill Revitalization and Affordable Commercial Program)
Overview: The council held a special meeting with a public hearing on 2023 midterm board and commission appointments, then appointed Hannah Davis and Greg Hill, Renee Golbeck and James Lindberg, Harmon Zuckerman, and Tell Jones to vacant seats by acclamation or vote. In the study session, staff presented revitalization strategies for the University Hill commercial area, including district-wide identity, connectivity, and activation efforts, plus a longer-term look at the 14th Street parking lot, and council generally supported prioritizing broad strategies and exploring liquor-rule code changes. Staff also presented a proposed affordable commercial pilot program developed with CU Boulder, and council supported moving forward with its exploration.

Topic1.Title: Public Hearing and Appointments to Boards and Commissions
Topic1.Summary: The city clerk outlined vacancies on the Environmental Advisory Board, Landmarks Board, Open Space Board of Trustees, and University Hill Commercial Area Management Commission. No one signed up to speak during the public hearing, which was closed. Council nominated and voted on candidates using the finalist process, with the rounds producing Hannah Davis, Greg Hill, Renee Golbeck, Harmon Zuckerman, and Tell Jones as appointees. Council then unanimously approved the slate.

Topic2.Title: University Hill Revitalization Strategies
Topic2.Summary: Staff presented history, regulations, safety concerns, a 14 percent commercial vacancy rate, and funding constraints for the University Hill General Improvement District. Recommendations included district identity work, improved connectivity along 13th Street, and activation efforts, with staff proposing to prioritize these before redeveloping the 14th Street lot. Council asked questions about the liquor rules, parking, and the Hill Hotel's impact, and members generally supported the broad strategies and exploring code changes.

Topic3.Title: Affordable Commercial Pilot Program
Topic3.Summary: Staff and CU Real Estate Center graduate students presented research on rising commercial lease costs in Boulder and peer programs in other cities. The proposal is a five-year pilot in which the city would master-lease space and sublease to small businesses and nonprofits at reduced operating costs, paired with free education, with a program administrator selected through an RFP. Council members raised questions about eligibility, sustainability, funding sources, and cost to the city, and generally supported continuing the exploration.
